subsystems.name: Converter stations
subsystems.role: the AC/DC interface at each end of the link.

subsystems.name: Overhead line
subsystems.role: the cheap, high-capacity land portion of the route.

subsystems.name: Submarine cable
subsystems.role: carries DC power under water, where overhead lines are impossible.

subsystems.name: DC protection and switching
subsystems.role: clears faults on a network where current has no natural zero crossing.

subsystems.name: Control and grid-forming systems
subsystems.role: keeps a converter-fed network stable without the inertia of spinning generators.

subsystems.name: Installation fleet
subsystems.role: lays and buries thousands of kilometres of cable.

buildSteps.title: Plan the route
buildSteps.detail: Map generation, demand and seabed bathymetry to pick corridors that balance cost, loss and environmental impact.

buildSteps.title: Survey the seabed
buildSteps.detail: Multibeam sonar and sub-bottom profiling identify cables crossings, trenches, wrecks and protected habitats.

buildSteps.title: Manufacture cable
buildSteps.detail: Conductor, insulation, moisture barrier and armour are built up in one continuous factory run, since a joint at sea is far more vulnerable than one on land.

buildSteps.title: Lay the submarine section
buildSteps.detail: A cable ship pays cable out under controlled tension; near shore a plough or jetting tool buries it below the seabed for protection from anchors and trawls.

buildSteps.title: Build the overhead section
buildSteps.detail: On land, towers and conductors are erected, or the route diverts underground through cable tunnels where land is scarce.

buildSteps.title: Construct converter stations
buildSteps.detail: Valve halls, transformers and filters are built at each terminus and connected to the existing AC grid.

buildSteps.title: Commission and test
buildSteps.detail: Power is ramped up, protection settings are proven, and converter controls are tuned to support the connected grids.

buildSteps.title: Operate as a network
buildSteps.detail: Trading and dispatch schedules move power between time zones, while converters provide voltage and frequency support as well as bulk transfer.

prerequisites.why: the only practical way to move bulk power thousands of kilometres with acceptable losses.
overhead DC lines above 3,000 km at up to 1,100 kV are already operating in China.
the longest subsea links now run roughly 700–800 km at around 525 kV using extruded insulation.

prerequisites.tech: Multi-terminal DC grids and DC breakers
prerequisites.why: point-to-point links dominate; switching faults on a meshed DC network is only now being proved at high voltage.
a converter-only grid has no rotating mass, so stability must be created electronically.
would be needed for links far longer than any submarine route currently built.

pathway.milestone: point-to-point HVDC links of a few gigawatts, mostly within one continent
pathway.unlocks: sharing power between neighbouring countries and moving offshore wind to shore.

pathway.milestone: multi-terminal DC hubs, such as the North Sea and Chinese meshed DC projects, connecting several countries at once
pathway.unlocks: the building blocks of a regional supergrid.

pathway.milestone: regional supergrids joining continents across short sea crossings
pathway.unlocks: using evening demand in one region to absorb midday solar from another.

pathway.milestone: intercontinental links carrying desert solar and high-latitude wind
pathway.unlocks: near-continuous renewable supply without relying on long-duration storage alone.

pathway.milestone: a planetary network of interlinked continental grids
pathway.unlocks: seasonal balancing across hemispheres — the technical limit is cable loss, not distance.
